svg.title: Preparation produces new bodily evidence
svg.desc: Panel A is an abstract diagram of selected primate pathways. Solid arrows run from orbital/medial prefrontal cortex to hypothalamus and from hypothalamus to the boundary of a brainstem/spinal autonomic group. A dashed arrow labeled peripheral effector pathways runs from that group to the body, shown with heart, vessel and gut icons. A dashed arrow labeled visceral evidence runs from the body to cranial nerve IX/X sensory afferents. Solid arrows continue from IX/X afferents to caudal NTS in the medulla and from caudal NTS to the parabrachial nuclei in the pons. A labeled gap separates the parabrachial nuclei from insular cortex; no arrow crosses it. Two offset solid arrows connect insular and orbital/medial prefrontal cortex in opposite directions. A key states that solid arrows are selected anatomical projections, dashed arrows summarize intervening steps, and only direction is shown. Panel B shows human experiments in separate participant groups. A schematic ECG timing guide marks diastole at the R-wave and systole about 300 ms after R, with the same fearful face at each marker. A detection task shows a compressed rapid stream at 70 ms per item, with a house target T1 and a fearful-face target T2 five items later in most trials, followed by identifying both the house and face targets; fear detection was greater at systole than diastole. A separate intensity task shows a fearful face for 100 ms, a fixation cross for 150 ms, a ready screen for 3 to 4 s, then a GO cue appearing simultaneously with the intensity-rating scale; fear intensity was greater at systole than diastole. Neutral faces were the comparison. Icons are illustrative.

g.text: T2: 5 items after T1 in most trials
